findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed run's armed baseline_suite/after_suite pair both ran at the head revision fa93ad50b — baseline_suite is the key-present arm (1 failed / 253 passed / 14 skipped) and after_suite the empty-key arm (1 failed / 208 passed / 59 skipped). Neither names the reviewed base c0c71ec3f, so the armed pair answers 'does the change add a failure' (0) but not 'what did the change repair'. The change's actual effect sits only in evidence_inputs: gate-emptykey-pre.log at the base (18 failed) against gate-after-emptykey.log at the head (1 failed), and gate-emptykey-pre.log carries no rev/cwd/cmd header line, so its revision claim is not readable from the log itself. Naming the base arm as baseline_suite would make the repaired-failure figure read directly from the armed pair, which is the convention the sibling review record (r-20261007T154229329439 review) follows.

follow-on: the two post-change gate logs the reviewed manifest cites (gate-after-emptykey.log, gate-after-keypresent.log) carry no FAILED line in pytest's short-summary section, so the failure id the manifest declares cannot be read from either log — only the progress marker (one F in tests/test_imas_search_scoring.py) and the mock traceback are present. This review reproduced the omission independently: the twelve-file arm at the head prints SKIPPED entries but no FAILED line, while running tests/test_imas_search_scoring.py alone DOES print 'FAILED tests/test_imas_search_scoring.py::TestCodeExampleVectorSearch::test_graceful_on_missing_index'. The declared id is correct (confirmed by the isolated run) but is not log-derivable, so a reader of the record cannot verify it without re-running. Cause not diagnosed here; it is pre-existing and independent of this change.

justifications.durability: The change is falsifiable and this review falsified the isolation it adds in the negative direction: removing the tests/discovery/test_judgment.py fixture and running that file with the key absent reddens exactly the two rerank tests the head arm does not fail (2 failed / 8 passed, EXIT=1), while the same file at the head with the fixture is 10 passed. That shows the fixture, not the environment, is what carries those tests. Marked down from perfect because the test_discover_map.py key is set inside the shared _patch_worker helper rather than a file-scoped autouse fixture, so a future test added to that module that drives the worker without the helper would silently measure the skip again, and because the fixture idiom is duplicated verbatim across four files (no single shared fixture), which will need re-applying if more files become key-dependent.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced, not read. Both reviewed revisions were extracted with git archive into $TMPDIR and every arm re-run there with module.__file__ under the scratch tree: base c0c71ec3f empty-key 18 failed / 191 passed / 59 skipped (review_base_emptykey.log), head fa93ad50b empty-key 1 failed / 208 passed / 59 skipped (review_head_emptykey.log, matching the reviewed after_suite exactly), head key-present 1 failed / 253 passed / 14 skipped (review_head_keypresent.log, matching the reviewed baseline_suite exactly), and the declared negative control 2 failed / 8 passed (review_negative_control.log). The base failure ids were enumerated authoritatively via junit XML (18 ids, base_junit.xml). Marked down because the reviewed manifest's own armed pair does not carry the base revision and the post-change gate logs omit the FAILED short-summary line, so the record's declared failure id and repaired-failure count cannot be read from the logs it cites without an independent run.
justifications.fit: Tests-only remediation that matches the prior review's recommendation (remediation in the test files) and the §8 intent that the tests keep exercising the rerank they replace. It extends the pattern already used elsewhere in the repository (a monkeypatch.setenv of the decisions key) rather than inventing a new mechanism, and it does not touch production code, so the key-absent skip behaviour decisions-key-skip landed is left exactly as reviewed.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Exactly reproduces the intended behaviour. On this review's reproduction of the head, with the key absent the seventeen previously-red tests are green and only the pre-existing key-independent failure remains; with the key present the same single failure remains and the skip-heavy arm is no longer reached. The change adds no failure in either arm (added_failure_count 0).
justifications.reuse: Reuses pytest's monkeypatch.setenv and the repository's existing decisions-key fixture idiom; no new helper module, no new production seam, no second spelling of the key handling. Uses the existing shared _patch_worker helper in test_discover_map.py rather than editing seven tests individually. Marked down slightly because the same three-line autouse fixture is written out four times across the files rather than shared, which is duplication a conftest-level fixture could remove.
justifications.scope_discipline: Five files changed, every one inside the declared write paths and none of production code: four test files and the evidence fragment, 118 insertions / 0 deletions. The reviewed run's declared scope was broader (eleven test paths) but only the four carrying key-dependent tests were touched, which is the tighter reading. No file outside the declared set appears in the diff.

raw_text: VERDICT goal: seventeen key-dependent tests across tests/cli/test_discover_map.py, tests/discovery/test_judgment.py, tests/ids/test_escalated_target_choice.py and tests/llm/test_search_tools.py now install their own dummy OPENROUTER_API_KEY_IMAS_CODEX via monkeypatch.setenv, so the twelve-file gate is green with the key absent except the one pre-existing, key-independent failure — the test-isolation remediation of the decision the decisions-key-skip review found. EVIDENCE: independently reproduced at base c0c71ec3f empty-key 18 failed / 191 passed / 59 skipped and at head fa93ad50b empty-key 1 failed / 208 passed / 59 skipped (matching the reviewed after_suite) and key-present 1 failed / 253 passed / 14 skipped (matching the reviewed baseline_suite); the declared negative control (test_judgment.py fixture removed) reproduces 2 failed / 8 passed. added_failure_count 0 against the reviewed node's own armed pair (both arms carry the same single failure id test_graceful_on_missing_index). SCOPE: five files, 118 insertions / 0 deletions, all declared, no production code. DURABILITY: the fixtures are load-bearing and their removal reddens exactly the two rerank tests; the sole mark-down is that test_discover_map.py sets the key in the shared helper rather than a file-scoped fixture, and the fixture is duplicated across four files. FIT: tests-only remediation following the prior review; extends the existing setenv idiom. REUSE: reuses monkeypatch.setenv and the shared worker helper. Follow-ons: the reviewed armed pair both runs at the head revision, so the repaired-failure figure lives in evidence_inputs (base 18 → head 1) rather than in the armed fields, and gate-emptykey-pre.log carries no rev/cwd/cmd header; and the post-change gate logs omit pytest's FAILED short-summary line so the declared failure id is not readable from them (confirmed correct by an isolated run of tests/test_imas_search_scoring.py).
